data.narrative:
EdgeRunner AI, a Series A defense and security company that has raised $17.5M to date, is evaluated against a comparative universe of 10 peers (2 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a value proxy, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $35M. Peer-median analysis across four same-stage, same-sector comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B), Castelion ($1.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—produces a median valuation of $700M, with a range spanning $125M to $4.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $30M (low) to $805M (high), with a median of $368M. The wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity within the defense AI peer set: NODA AI sits at $125M while Stark Defence commands $4.0B, a 32x differential. Stage-progression anchors a floor near current capital deployed, while peer-median carries substantial upside optionality but depends heavily on whether EdgeRunner's competitive positioning and technology differentiation align with higher-valued peers. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, technology defensibility, and the degree to which defense sector demand tailwinds justify valuations at the upper end of the peer range.
